title: Every Kid Outdoors: Free National Park Pass for 4th Graders
description: US fourth graders can get a free Every Kid Outdoors pass covering national park entrance fees for the family. How to get the 2026–27 pass and what it covers.
h1: Every Kid Outdoors: a free national parks pass for fourth graders
intro: If you have a fourth grader in the US, your whole family can visit national parks and other federal lands without paying entrance fees for a year. Here’s how.

image.alt: Deer grazing in a meadow below Half Dome in Yosemite

cardText: Free entry to US national parks for the whole family, thanks to your fourth grader.

blocks.title: Scout’s pass tip
blocks.text: The 2026–27 pass is valid from 1 September 2026 to 31 August 2027, so the sooner you get it, the more trips you can squeeze in.
points: Complete a short activity on the website
Swap it for a pass at a participating site if you want a durable card

sections.html: US fourth-grade students, including home-schooled children of fourth-grade age (usually 10), can get the pass for the school year. The programme has been reauthorised through 2031.

1. Visit everykidoutdoors.gov with your child.
  2. Complete the short educational activity.
  3. Download and print the voucher (check the site for the current digital pass option).
  4. Show it at federal recreation sites, or exchange it for a durable pass.

It covers entrance fees at more than 2,000 federal sites. At per-vehicle sites, that’s the car and its passengers. At per-person sites, it covers all children under 16 plus up to three adults. It doesn’t cover camping, parking, tours or boat trips.
Our guide to US national parks with kids has Junior Ranger tips and planning ideas.

faqs.q: When does the 2026–27 Every Kid Outdoors pass expire?
faqs.a: The 2026–27 pass is valid from 1 September 2026 to 31 August 2027.

faqs.q: Does the Every Kid Outdoors pass cover camping?
faqs.a: No. It covers entrance and standard day-use fees, not camping, parking, tours or other expanded amenity fees.
